draft.title: Classical conditioning
card: Classical conditioning is learning by association. Two stimuli are paired until one comes to trigger a response it did not trigger before.
Before conditioning
an unconditioned stimulus (UCS) causes an unconditioned response (UCR) without any learning. A neutral stimulus (NS) causes no such response.
During conditioning
the NS is presented just before the UCS, again and again. The UCS keeps causing the UCR.
After conditioning
the NS is now a conditioned stimulus (CS). It causes a conditioned response (CR) on its own, and the CR is usually similar to the UCR.
draft.remember: Pair a neutral stimulus with a UCS, and it becomes a CS that causes a CR.

a.q: A dog gets food (UCS) and drools (UCR). A bell is rung just before the food each time. After many trials, the bell alone makes the dog drool. What is the bell now?
opts: A conditioned stimulus
An unconditioned stimulus
A conditioned response
An unconditioned response
a.why: The bell began as a neutral stimulus. After being paired with the food, it causes drooling on its own, so it is a conditioned stimulus. It is not the unconditioned stimulus, because the food still plays that role and needs no learning.
a.clue: The bell started out neutral and then was learned.

b.q: Mia hears a dentist's drill (NS) just before each painful jab (UCS) that makes her flinch. Later, the drill alone makes her flinch. Which pair is correct?
opts: The jab is the UCS and the flinch at the drill is the CR
The drill is the UCS and the flinch at the jab is the CR
The jab is the CS and the flinch at the drill is the UCR
The drill is the CS and the flinch at the jab is the CR
b.why: The pain of the jab causes a flinch without learning, so it is the UCS. The flinch to the drill alone is learned, so it is the CR. The tempting option calls the flinch at the drill a UCR, but a response to a learned stimulus is conditioned.
b.clue: Which stimulus causes the flinch without any learning?

b.best: The jab is the UCS and the flinch at the drill is the CR

problems.detail: The stem already labels the jab as the UCS, and only one option calls the jab the UCS. A student can match the label and pick the right option without understanding conditioning.

Why (b) names 'the flinch at the drill is the UCR' as the tempting option. That option also calls the jab the CS, so it is easily ruled out. The more tempting distractor is 'The drill is the CS and the flinch at the jab is the CR', and the why does not explain why that one is wrong.

check.summary: The card and question a are accurate. Question b gives its answer away, because the stem labels the jab as the UCS and only one option matches that label. Its why also skips the most tempting wrong option.
